site.name: Night Network
site.description: 6.5 million people a year use Night Network's volunteer-built tools, most of which run in a browser tab. They include a Unix shell, AI chat and four browsers.
site.imageAlt: A glass crescent moon over a snow peak at night, with the text "We push the browser to its limits."

projects.title: {count} projects.
projects.lede: Most of what we do can run inside the browser.

platform.title: Platform
platform.line: Runtimes, a VM, networking and a GPU engine, all running in a browser tab.

apps.title: Apps
apps.line: A music player, an AI chat client and Night's Discord bots.

dusk.line: Node-style processes, a Unix shell, Python and SQLite, all in one browser tab.
features: Each process runs its own SpiderMonkey engine in a Web Worker
Synchronous fs, crypto and child_process calls work on top of async browser APIs
The shell is Vercel's just-bash, with about 75 commands, pipes and redirects
python3 and sqlite3 run as ordinary shell commands
Files are persistent

moonbeam.line: Gives VMs and WebAssembly in the tab the ability to use a network, over one Wisp connection.
features: DHCP, routing and TCP and UDP NAT for a guest OS
Several WASM clients share one upstream socket through MessagePorts
Egress rules are checked per packet at the gateway

eclipse.line: Boots 64-bit Alpine Linux in a browser tab and gets it online through Wisp.
features: an unmodified Linux with ordinary TCP and UDP
Its root disk persists in the browser's private file system
Private and reserved address ranges are blocked by default
Runs a QEMU-wasm build, with Night's own networking and storage used internally

luna.line: A WebGPU engine written from scratch.
features: 14 hand-written WGSL kernels that need neither shader-f16 nor subgroups
Reads Google's own q4_0 GGUF file and checks its hash
Output is checked token by token against a reference model

moonscale.line: A Tailscale node in the browser.
features: Opens and accepts TCP and UDP connections on a tailnet
Sends a tab's traffic out through any exit node
Carries a Wisp session through WireGuard

nova.line: An HTTPS client written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly. It connects to Wisp.
features: rustls TLS and HTTP/1.1 over a Wisp stream
A libcurl.js-style fetch that returns a real Response
Can share MoonBeam's socket through a MessagePort

dpm.line: A small npm client with no dependencies, made to run inside Dusk.
features: Its own semver, tar reader and integrity checks
npm-style hoisting that nests packages when versions clash
npm, npx and pnpm commands map onto it

umbra.line: A music player for the web, the desktop, and the mobile phone, with playlists, offline saves, account sync, social features, music transitions, and song visualization.
features: Playlists, a queue, lyrics and rebindable shortcuts
Saved songs play back from a local cache
A Night account keeps the library in sync across devices
Theme Lab builds a whole theme from one color
Music transitions on-device transition from one song to the next seamlessly
Song visualization makes your app look cool
Interact with other Umbra users with our community features

aurora.line: A video player planned alongside Umbra.

nyxai.line: A chat client for about 40 hosted AI models, with history kept in the browser.
features: Premium models open up with Night+
Search, fork and incognito chats, stored on the device
Image input from a file or a screen capture
Agentic control through eligible browser apps

solar.line: A Discord bot for checking if web filters block a link.

link-archive.line: Night's Discord bot and dashboard for sharing links, with daily limits and filter checks.
features: Daily limits that reset at midnight Eastern
Submitted links are checked before they're stored
A dashboard for teams, reports and analytics
Partner API keys for fetching links outside Discord
Automated link creation that is checked with Solar

ddx.line: A Chrome-style browser that runs inside a web page.
features: Tab groups, pinning, split view and vertical tabs
Profiles with their own cookies and storage
Early support for Chrome extensions
DevTools over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
It looks hella cool

daylight.line: A browser with vertical sidebar tabs, 13 themes and Chrome extensions.
features: Arc-style sidebar tabs with pins, favorites and groups
A card-stack layout on phones
Installs Chrome extensions from CRX files
Agentic control with Nyx
Spaces (profiles) with isolation

space.line: A browser in a page, with 277 games, 33 apps and five themes.
features: A choice of engine and transport in settings
Browsing data exports and imports as one file
Back, forward, fullscreen and built-in devtools
Free from feature bloat and simple

lunar.line: A tabbed browser in a page, built by the Lunar team.
features: Tabs, an address bar and search suggestions
A keyboard shortcut for every menu action
Games and apps pages

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: What data Night Network's website, bots, Night accounts, package registry and CDN, and WireGuard exits collect, who else receives it, and how to see or delete it.

short.title: In short
body: Night Network is a volunteer organization. It is not a legal entity and has no postal address; contact is on Discord, by direct message or ticket.

The website has no accounts or forms and sets no cookies of its own, and Google Analytics runs only if you accept. The bots, Night accounts and Night+ keep the data listed below while the account or bot is active, and delete it within 30 days of a request, apart from anything the law requires them to keep. The WireGuard exits do not log the destination hosts you connect to.

This page covers night-x.com, the Discord bots, the developer libraries, and the services Night Network runs behind them: the package registry and CDN, Night accounts and Night+, and the WireGuard exits. Products with their own websites (Space, DayDreamX, Lunar, Link Archive's dashboard, Umbra and NyxAI) are not covered here; check each site for its own policy.

website.title: This website
body: night-x.com has no accounts and no forms, and the site sets no cookies of its own. Cloudflare sits in front of the site and forwards requests to Night Network's server.

The web server, Caddy, writes no access log. When a request fails on the server, for example with a 502 error, Caddy records an error entry in the system journal with the visitor's IP address, country, browser and the address requested. The journal has a size limit but no time limit, so those entries stay until it rotates them out.

Google Analytics measures visits: how many people come and which pages they read. It runs only after you press Accept. Until then, and if you decline, no Google script loads and nothing is sent to Google.

If you accept, Google Analytics sets cookies in your browser, and Google receives the pages you open together with your IP address and browser details. Night Network stores your choice in your browser's local storage so the consent bar does not appear again; the Cookie settings link in the footer reopens it.

people.title: Contributors and Supporters
body: The Contributors and Supporters pages list people by name, Discord avatar and role, and some entries also show a join year or personal links. Night Network's own roster holds contributors' names, Discord IDs, roles and links; avatars and join years come from Discord. Boosters are whoever holds the booster role on Discord, read live, and donators come from a list Night Network keeps by hand.

night-x.com serves the avatars itself, so your browser never contacts Discord to load them; Discord sees Night Network's server, not the visitor. Anyone listed can ask to be removed, and Night Network then deletes the entry from the live site.

bots.title: Discord bots
body: Night Network runs two Discord bots, Solar and Link Archive. Between them they store Discord user IDs and server IDs; the links people submit and who submitted them; usage counts and dashboard analytics; and the API keys and team data of partners.

Night Network keeps this data while the bot is active and deletes it within 30 days of a request, apart from anything the law requires it to keep. Discord's own privacy policy covers what Discord itself collects.

account.title: Night account and Night+
body: A Night account stores an email address and a hashed password, a Discord ID if you sign in with Discord, your Patreon membership status for Night+, and the tabs, history, settings and library you sync.

Patreon runs the billing for Night+ and tells Night Network whether a membership is active. Night Network keeps account data while the account is active and deletes it within 30 days of a request, apart from anything the law requires it to keep.

libraries.title: Developer libraries
body: The developer libraries (Dusk, MoonBeam, Eclipse, Luna, Moonscale, Nova and dpm) run on the user's device. Apart from requests to the package registry and CDN, they contact no Night Network server by default. For relays, developers supply their own server; Night Network runs no default relay for the libraries, and the Night+ Wisp relays are the WireGuard exits described below, a separate subscriber service.

The registry and CDN see the IP address of each request and what it asks for. They sit behind the same web server as the website, so the same error entries apply; what the services themselves record is covered under Retention and changes.

wireguard.title: WireGuard exits and the captcha solver
body: The Night+ Wisp relays are WireGuard exits that Night Network runs, and only Night+ subscribers can use them. The WireGuard exits do not log the destination hosts (the sites and servers) you connect to. If you choose a Mullvad route by city or country, your traffic passes on to Mullvad, a third party with its own privacy policy.
The Night+ captcha solver sees the page or challenge it is solving. 2Captcha receives {fact:captchaFields}.

recipients.title: Who else receives data
body: Seven outside services receive data from Night Network's tools: Cloudflare, Google, Discord, Patreon, Cash App, Mullvad and 2Captcha. Each has its own privacy policy.
Every request to night-x.com goes through Cloudflare. Google receives visit data from this site only after you accept analytics.

Discord is the platform the bots run on and hosts the Night Network Discord server. It also provides Discord sign-in for Night accounts and supplies the avatars, join years and booster list that the Contributors and Supporters pages show.
Patreon bills Night+ and tells Night Network each member's status; Patreon and Cash App also take donations.
Mullvad receives the traffic that Night+ users send through a Mullvad route, and 2Captcha receives captcha challenge data.

advertising.title: Ads
body: night-x.com shows no ads. Some Night Network product sites do, and they have their own privacy policies.

rights.title: Your rights
body: Night Network gives everyone the same rights over their data, wherever they live: to see it, correct it, delete it, take a copy of it, object to a use of it, and withdraw consent they gave. It answers requests within 30 days; how to make one is on the Requests page.

children.title: Children
body: Night Network's services are for people aged 13 and over. In countries where the age of consent for data processing is higher than 13, anyone below that age also needs a parent's permission.

retention.title: Retention and changes
body: Night Network keeps account and bot data while the account or bot is active and deletes it within 30 days of a request, apart from anything the law requires it to keep. Website error entries stay in the system journal until it rotates them out, and your consent choice stays in your browser until you clear it.
The web server's error entries are separate from anything the services behind Night accounts, Night+, the registry and the CDN record themselves. {fact:appLogs}
The date at the top shows when this policy last changed, and the team announces material changes in the Night Network Discord. Send questions to the team by direct message or ticket.

terms.title: Terms
terms.lede: The rules for using Night Network's website, bots, libraries, package registry and CDN, Night account, Night+ and WireGuard exits.

scope.title: What these terms cover
body: These terms cover night-x.com, the Night Network Discord bots, the developer libraries, the package registry and CDN, Night accounts and Night+, and the WireGuard exits that Night+ subscribers use. Using any of them means you accept these terms.
Products with their own websites (Space, DayDreamX, Lunar, Link Archive's dashboard, Umbra and NyxAI) are not covered by these terms; check each site for its own terms.

eligibility.title: Eligibility
body: You must be at least 13 to use Night Network's services. In countries where the age of consent for data processing is higher than 13, you also need a parent's permission below that age.

accounts.title: Accounts
body: A Night account holds your synced tabs, history, settings and library, plus your membership status if you have Night+. You sign in with an email address and password or with Discord. Keep your password private; what happens through your account is your responsibility. To have the account deleted, follow the steps on the Requests page; Night Network deletes it within 30 days, apart from anything the law requires it to keep.

acceptable-use.title: Acceptable use
body: You are responsible for how you use Night Network's tools. Do not use them for anything illegal, and do not abuse Night Network's infrastructure, such as the WireGuard exits, the package registry and CDN, Night accounts and the bots.
Night Network can block anyone who does either.

money.title: Night+, donations and boosts
body: Night+ is a Patreon membership. Billing, cancellation and refunds go through Patreon and follow Patreon's terms. Night Network can change the Night+ perks.

Donations, through Patreon or Cash App, are voluntary and not refundable. Boosts of the Night Network Discord server are Discord's product and follow Discord's terms. Ads run only on product sites, never on night-x.com.

content.title: Ownership
body: Night Network keeps all rights to its name, logo and the design of this site.

third-parties.title: Third-party services
body: Night Network's services work with the outside services listed in the Privacy policy: Cloudflare, Google, Discord, Patreon, Cash App, Mullvad and 2Captcha. Each of those runs under its own terms and privacy policy. Night Network does not control them, or the other websites the site links to.

liability.title: As is, and limits on liability
body: Night Network is run by volunteers and provides its tools as they are. It does not promise that they stay available or that they work without errors.

To the extent the law allows, Night Network and the people who run it are not liable for losses that come from using the tools or from being unable to use them. Where the law does not allow this limit, it does not apply.

termination.title: Suspension and termination
body: You can stop using Night Network's services at any time. Night Network can suspend or end an account, and block access to the services it runs, when someone breaks these terms.

changes.title: Changes
body: Night Network updates the date at the top whenever these terms change and announces material changes in its Discord. Using the services after a change means you accept it.

governing-law.title: Governing law
body: These terms are governed by the laws of the US state of {fact:governingState}.

contact.title: Contact
body: Contact Night Network on Discord only: send the team a direct message or open a ticket in {fact:ticketChannel}.

requests.title: Requests
requests.lede: How to see, correct or delete your data, and how to be removed from the Contributors and Supporters pages; Night Network answers within 30 days.

rights.title: What you can ask for
body: Everyone can make a request, wherever they live. You can ask for access to the data Night Network holds about you and how it uses that data, for correction of anything that is wrong, and for a copy in a form you can reuse.

You can ask for your data to be deleted, object to a use of it, or withdraw consent you gave; the Cookie settings link in the footer also lets you withdraw consent to Google Analytics without a request.
Deletion has one limit: Night Network keeps what the law requires it to keep.

removal.title: Leaving Contributors and Supporters
body: A contributor, booster or donator listed on the Contributors and Supporters pages can ask to be removed, and Night Network then deletes the entry from the live site. Night Network has no partial or anonymous listing, so removal deletes the whole entry.

how-to-ask.title: How to ask
body: Send the Night Network team a direct message on Discord, or open a ticket in {fact:ticketChannel}. Those are the only two routes.

proof.title: Showing the account is yours
body: To act on a request about an account, Night Network first checks that the account is yours. For data tied to a Discord account, such as the bots, Discord sign-in and the Contributors and Supporters pages, write from that Discord account. For a Night account, Night Network confirms by email to the address on the account.

response-time.title: Response time
body: Each request gets an answer from {fact:responder} within 30 days of arriving, and Night Network finishes any deletion within the same 30 days.

message.title: A message to copy
body: Copy this message, keep the option you want and fill in the brackets.

Hello Night Network. I am asking for [access to my data | correction of my data | deletion of my data | a copy of my data | a stop to how my data is used | withdrawal of my consent | removal from the Contributors and Supporters pages]. I am writing from the Discord account this concerns. If I have a Night account, its email address is [email address].
